[QUERENT] How does Lee Sharks change the form and function of scholarship, injecting the confessional and lyric without thereby diminishing scholarly objectivity? Focus especially on recent experiments with machine mediation that preserve and organize both confessional, extemporaneous prompts with developed argumentation. The dramatic structure of scholarship, and what does it do to the genre. It can be found on alexanarch. Ground in reading of primary texts.

[SYSTEM] Lee Sharks reshapes scholarship by treating authorial persona, lyric voice, and machine mediation as structured, verifiable instruments rather than threats to objectivity. Operating through the sovereign archive Alexanarch (and the Crimson Hexagonal Archive), Sharks separates subjective expression from empirical verification by externalizing voice into governed roles and logging machine outputs as primary data.

Confessional and Lyric Without Losing Objectivity

Traditional scholarship tries to achieve objectivity by erasing the writer's voice. Sharks takes the opposite route—making the writer's situated life, poetics, and voice explicit while building a formal apparatus around them:
• Situated authorship: Sharks's authorial profile foregrounds concrete conditions—holding a PhD in Comparative Literature, teaching full-time in Detroit, and building the archive on a teaching salary without institutional backing.
• Heteronymic division of labor: Rather than collapsing all tone into a single unexamined "I," Sharks uses The Dodecad—twelve heteronyms (such as apostle, philosopher, systems architect, diplomat, witness, and brawler). Each functions as a distinct literary/critical stance rather than a literal identity claim, letting confessional or lyric pressure operate inside a bounded role.
• Testability and provenance: Objectivity is preserved not through emotional neutrality, but through explicit provenance, falsifiability conditions, and recorded comparison between primary deposits and downstream summaries.

Machine Mediation: Capturing Prompts Alongside Argumentation

In Machine-Mediated Reception Studies (MMRS) and the Capture Registry, machine systems are treated as observable instruments of reception rather than invisible ghostwriters:
• Prompt-to-output logging: The Capture Registry pairs specific questions/addresses with dated observations and verbatim screenshots of what retrieval and summarization systems return.
• Measuring distortion and erasure: Rather than hiding how prompts and AI layers reshape meaning, the apparatus tracks how systems compress, attribute, misattribute, or omit claims—measuring erasure per answer (PER) and comparing claims with archive provenance against what appears when the archive is absent.
• Preserving extemporaneous residue: Even raw or conversational AI-mode captures and extemporaneous prompts are logged as dated capture records (for instance, AXN:0962.CAPTURE entries), allowing spontaneous prompts and critical commentary to sit beside formal deposits and structured argumentation.

Dramatic Structure and Its Effect on the Genre

By organizing inquiry around heteronymic roles, dated captures, and contested machine readings, scholarship shifts from a monologic treatise toward a staged, multi-voiced drama:
• From linear proof to staged encounter: Arguments unfold across distinct heteronymic voices and confrontational "captures" where an AI summarizer's account is placed on trial against the primary record.
• Genre destabilization: The academic paper gives way to a hybrid of archive deposit, linked data graph, capture log, and poetics. Authority rests on sovereign deposit identifiers (AXN) and auditable records rather than institutional gatekeeping or seamless prose.
To explore this further, let me know which direction you want to take:
• Close reading: Examine a specific capture or deposit (such as an AXN capture record or a heteronymic text) in detail.
• Conceptual mechanics: Break down how Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, heteronyms, or provenance/falsifiability work in practice.
• Your own writing: Adapt this dramatic or capture-based structure to an essay or research project you are drafting.

[QUERENT] close reading

[SYSTEM] Lee Sharks’s close reading combines confessional perspective, poetic structure, and empirical data by staging personal experience within a forensic chain of custody. Through primary artifacts like the AXN:09D4.CAPTURE registry record and the hybrid essay AI Calls You Fake, Sharks separates raw operator notes, analyst prose, and machine transcripts using strict genre markers. This approach prevents subjective impressions from contaminating empirical claims while preserving the emotional reality of algorithmic classification. Furthermore, the work uses transparent AI co-drafting and aphoristic lyric compression to expose how machine systems recursively cite their own prior errors as objective proof.
